question: Which social reformer founded the Satyashodhak Samaj?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Jyotirao Phule**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jyotiba Phule established the Satyashodhak Samaj**, a social reform organization, on September 24, 1873,** in Pune, Maharashtra.**
 
• It advocated for the empowerment of marginalized people through education and greater political and social access, paying particular attention to women, peasants, and Dalits in Maharashtra.
 
• **Savitribai**, the **wife of Jyotirao**, presided over the society's female division.
 
• The Samaj dissolved in the 1930s as its leaders left to join the **Indian National Congress party.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Objectives of Satyashodhak Samaj**

 
 
• **​**Stop **Brahmins **from taking advantage of **Dalits, ati-Shudras, or Shudras.**
 
• Convincing and influencing everyone to think that they are **omnipotent's children**. Therefore, everyone must submit to and obey a single God.
 
• Claiming and establishing that no medium or means of communication with God is required. Phule further argued that every prayer subject and voice originates with the almighty before spreading through any channel to the outside world.
 
 
 
• **Oath and affirmations of** Satyashodhak Samaj
 
 
• ​It is essential that persons from **lower castes have access to education.**
 
• Promoting cottage enterprises and the value of products made in the **India.**
 
• Destroying the long-established **social status of Brahmins.**
